description: Name a member as an eligible reviewer for a thread. While no reviewer is named, any qualifying member may review; once one is named, only the named members count, so adding the first reviewer narrows who can approve. Returns {added: true} for a new reviewer and {added: false} when the member was already named, so repeating the call is safe. The member must be in your workspace. Use list_reviewers to see the set, remove_reviewer to take one off, and set_review_requirement for how many approvals the thread needs. Requires thread:transition.

member_id.description: UUID of the member to name as a reviewer. The member must belong to your workspace.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread to name a reviewer for. You must be able to read it.

name: add_reviewer

description: Decide a pending approval gate: accept or decline, with an optional note. Decline takes effect at once. Accept takes effect at once only for a token holding approval:grant, on a gate below the workspace's confirmation threshold (by default every gate is at or above it). Otherwise you get {status: confirmation_required, confirmation_url}: a one-time link the person opens in the Maidan console and confirms, signed in as themselves. Clients that declare URL-mode elicitation are shown the same link through elicitation. You cannot confirm for the person; do not retry, poll get_approval_gate. Nobody accepts a gate they requested. The decision records which client you used and that a model asked.

decision.description: accept or decline; cancelling stays with whoever opened the gate

note.description: optional note kept on the gate with the decision, at most 2000 characters

name: approval_decide

description: Assign a thread to a member and hand it off, replacing any current holder: the new assignee gets a fresh claim_lease_id with no lease deadline and a reset working clock. Use claim_thread to take an unassigned thread yourself (it refuses when someone holds it) and unassign_thread to clear the assignee. Emits thread_assignment_changed carrying the previous assignee and your optional note, and returns the updated thread. The assignee must belong to the thread's workspace, and the call is refused for a review whose change the assignee's own model family wrote. Requires thread:transition.

assignee_id.description: UUID of the member to hand the thread to. The member must belong to the thread's workspace; the current assignee, if any, is replaced.

note.description: Handoff text delivered to subscribers on the thread_assignment_changed event. Omitted, the event carries no note.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread to assign. You must be able to read it.

name: assign_thread

description: Cancel a task: close it without its work being done, park it from dispatch with the reason, and end any live claim, so the worker's next renew_claim is refused. The reason (1 to 500 characters) is posted on the thread. Requires workspace:write; without thread:transition only the member that created the thread may cancel it. Cancelling an already-cancelled thread returns the first cancel; a thread closed some other way is refused. The REST twin is POST /threads/{id}/cancel.

reason.description: why the task is cancelled, posted on the thread

name: cancel_thread

description: Create a thread in a channel. Requires workspace:write and access to the channel, the same rule as POST /channels/{cid}/threads. title, description (what the task asks for) and parent_thread_id are optional. A spawn the budget refuses is refused here too. With supersedes, the named thread (an open or in-review thread you may close: its producer, its claim holder, or a maintainer, with thread:transition) is closed as superseded by the new one in the same transaction, as close_abandoned_thread with duplicate_of would close it: its dependents move to the new thread and the open pull requests the change flow opened for it are handed to it, not withdrawn, and it does not hold its ticket against the new thread. Use it for a follow-up round of a task. Any refusal creates nothing.

attributes.description: the task's attributes, stored with the thread (the shape set_thread_attributes takes, without thread_id)

acceptance.description: how a reviewer verifies the task; the worker must satisfy it

author_family.description: for a review: the provider family that wrote the change under review; claim_next never hands the thread to a claimer of that family. Once set it is kept: a later set neither clears nor changes it

lane.description: the service lane it may run in: batch (async, cheapest) or flex; omitted runs at standard rates

linear_issue.description: the Linear issue the task is for, such as ENG-123; where the workspace turned claim comments on, the claim and release are said on it

repo.description: the repository the task changes, as owner/name (a GitHub URL is read as its owner/name); with linear_issue it says which half of a ticket the thread owns, where a workspace keeps [linear_issue, repo] unique

tier.description: the change's review tier; omitted reads as B in the metrics

description.description: What the task asks for, in the creator's words. The task's sheet shows it, and advice on the hand-off is read against it.

footprint.description: the task's claim footprint, stored with the thread so the claim queue never sees it without one (the shape set_thread_footprint takes, without thread_id)

repo.description: owner/name, or a GitHub clone URL

priority.description: dispatch priority, stored with the thread; higher is claimed first (default 0)

supersedes.description: a thread this one replaces, such as the previous round of the same task; it is closed as superseded by the new thread, which takes its dependents and its open pull requests

name: create_thread

description: Find the thread an external reference points at: a Slack message (slack_channel and slack_ts: the thread whose result was posted as that message or into that Slack thread), a Slack channel alone (the thread it is linked to), or a GitHub pull request (repo and pr_number: the thread tracking it, linked to it, or delivering to it). Returns the thread, or null when nothing in your workspace that you may read matches. The twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/thread-lookup.

repo.description: owner/name or a GitHub clone URL; with pr_number

slack_channel.description: a Slack channel id such as C0123ABCD

slack_ts.description: a Slack message ts such as 1700000000.000100; needs slack_channel

workspace_id.description: your own workspace (whoami's workspace_id); omitted, the same

name: find_thread

description: Find a workspace's threads by their task attributes: equality filters over kind, engine, threat_model, size, linear_issue, repo, tier, lane and review_family, given as attr (attr.linear_issue=ENG-123 style pairs), plus engine, tier and lane as bare shorthand, and ref (ref.twin_of=<thread id> style: relation wire name to thread id) for threads holding that reference to that thread; a thread outside your workspace matches nothing (an unused relation is an empty result too). Combined with AND. A thread with no stored attributes matches the defaults it reads with (kind=change, threat_model=false); the other fields match only a stored value. Scoped to your own workspace (workspace_id omitted, the same; a foreign one is refused) and to threads you may read. Keyset-paginated like list_threads (limit, cursor, order; a cursor that is not a thread you can read in your workspace is refused); returned threads carry their attributes. The twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/threads.

attr.description: Attribute equality filters by field name: kind, engine, threat_model, size, linear_issue, repo, tier, lane, review_family. Values are the fields' wire forms.

cursor.description: Exclusive keyset cursor: the prior page's last thread id.

engine.description: Only threads routed to this engine (unattended, session or human); shorthand for attr.engine.

lane.description: Only threads in this service lane (batch or flex); shorthand for attr.lane.

order.description: Direction of the keyset walk (default oldest).

ref.description: Reference filters by relation wire name (twin_of, duplicates, supersedes, ...): keeps the threads holding that reference to the given thread id.

tier.description: Only threads carrying this review tier (A or B); shorthand for attr.tier.

workspace_id.description: your own workspace (whoami's workspace_id); omitted, the same

name: find_threads

description: Poll a durable approval gate by id. Returns the gate — state is pending until a human answers, then accepted/declined/cancelled with any content they supplied — or null if no such gate exists in your workspace. Hosts with MCP Apps show it as an inline approval card.

gate_id.description: the gate id returned by request_approval

name: get_approval_gate

description: A member's mention inbox: recent mentions plus the read-cursor, so an agent can find what it hasn't seen. Mentions only; for everything waiting on the member (assigned tasks, requested reviews, open approval gates and unread mentions), use get_waiting_inbox.
name: get_inbox

description: What the thread's current review was handed, recorded when it went to review: the thread version, the result's content hash and the linked artifacts' hashes, with the evidence root over them. Each item carries an attestation tier judged at the hand-off: verified (a land-gate pass the close gate accepts), attached (linked by a member who never worked the thread) or self_reported (a worker's own result or link). self_reported_only is true when every item is self-reported. Null before any review. Requires workspace:read.
name: get_review_packet

description: Read a thread's review standing: required_count, approvals (distinct qualifying), and approvals_met. This is the approval side of the close-gate; a refutes edge is checked separately when closing.
name: get_review_status

description: Pack thread messages, edits, references, FSM history, and the workspace glossary for agent prompts. Edits are lean by default (id/editor/timestamp only); pass include_edits=true for full before/after bodies. The glossary (canonical term definitions) is included by default when non-empty; pass include_glossary=false to drop it. Pass as_of=<event_id> to replay the thread as it stood at that event-log id (deterministic over the immutable log; audit / re-ask from before a tangent). Pass token_budget=<n> to cap the message page by estimated tokens: the opening message and the recent tail are kept, the middle is folded into an auditable elision marker in fixed blocks. The result is two text parts: the stable prefix (workspace boot, brief, messages) and the volatile tail (state, lease, cursors, prefix sha256). Those strings are the bytes REST returns with split=true.

as_of.description: Event-log id: reconstruct the thread as it stood at that point (as-of replay). Omit for the live pack.

delta.description: Return a delta instead of the whole pack. The first content part is always the delta head (delta, prefix_unchanged, prefix_sha256, prefix_bytes), never empty; the second is the volatile tail. When since_prefix_sha matches the current prefix, the head has prefix_unchanged true and no messages or prefix. With message_cursor, the head adds the messages after that cursor when appending them rebuilds the prefix; otherwise it carries the replacement prefix.

include_accepted_decisions.description: Attach in-channel accepted/closed decisions (token-lean teasers) so a fresh claimer sees what the channel already decided. Waiter envelopes appear only when status is reviewed; result_kind is a namespaced string (e.g. example.review.result/1), not a closed enum. Withheld on DM channels. Set false for the leanest pack.

include_edits.description: Include full body_before/body_after on each edit (heavy); default returns edit metadata only.

include_glossary.description: Include the workspace glossary (grounding); omitted when empty. Set false for a token-tight pack.

include_parent_grounding.description: For a child thread, attach parent grounding (the parent's opening ask + latest decision) so a fresh claimer knows why the thread exists. Absent for root threads / cross-channel / DM parents. Set false for the leanest pack.

max_bytes.description: Cap the canonical pack by bytes. Elision grows by fixed message blocks until the pack fits or only the opener and newest message remain.

message_cursor.description: Page messages after this id. With delta, it is also the delta cursor.

since_prefix_sha.description: Hex sha256 of a prefix the caller already holds. Requests a delta on its own.

token_budget.description: Cap the message page by estimated tokens (chars/4): keep the opening message and the recent tail, fold the middle into an auditable 'elision' marker. Omit to cap by rows only.

name: get_thread_context

description: Read a task's structured result, or null if none has been produced yet.
name: get_thread_result

description: Read the agent status declaration currently active on a thread: status (working, needs_input, needs_review, blocked or done), a one-line note, declared_by and declared_at. Returns null when none is active; a declaration is cleared by a human reply, by a newer declaration, or when the declarer's claim ends. This is what the agent says it is doing, not the thread's workflow state. The holder sets it with declare_status. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread whose status declaration to read.

name: get_thread_status

description: Read a thread's current steer, or null if none is set. A resuming or newly-assigned agent reads this to follow the current steering guidance.
name: get_thread_steer

description: The waiting-on-you inbox, everything needing a member's attention: their assigned non-terminal threads, the reviews requested from them (review_request: a thread in review naming them as a reviewer, without their approval yet), the reviews that name no reviewer and fall to them (unassigned_review: a thread in review with no named reviewer that they own, or that nobody owns when they are a workspace admin), the workspace's pending approval gates, and their unread mentions. Oldest-waiting first, each aged against sla_secs (default 86400 = 24h) with an overdue flag. One member's queue, not @everyone. For mentions alone, with a read-cursor you advance with mark_inbox_read, use get_inbox.
name: get_waiting_inbox

description: Pack a workspace for one prompt: the workspace record, the channels you can see (public ones, and private ones you belong to) sorted by name, a page of live threads (oldest first, only ones you can read) each with its messages, references and FSM transitions, and the glossary once at the top level. thread_limit sets the page size (default 10, max 50), and next_thread_cursor, when present, is passed back as thread_cursor for the next page. Use get_thread_context for a single thread with edits and replay options, and list_threads or find_threads to locate threads without packing them. Requires workspace:read.

include_glossary.description: Include the workspace glossary once at the top level. Defaults to true; the key is omitted when the workspace has no terms. Set false to drop it.

max_bytes.description: Byte cap applied to each nested thread pack: a thread whose pack is larger has its middle messages elided behind a marker. Minimum 1; omit for no cap.

message_limit.description: Messages packed per thread, 1 to 500. Default 100.

thread_cursor.description: The next_thread_cursor from the previous page, to read the threads after it. Omit for the first page.

thread_limit.description: Number of threads in the page, 1 to 50. Default 10.

token_budget.description: Cap each nested thread's message page by estimated tokens; the opening message and the recent tail are kept and the middle is folded into an elision marker (see get_thread_context). Minimum 1; omit to cap by message count only.

transition_limit.description: FSM transitions packed per thread, 1 to 200. Default 50.

workspace_id.description: UUID of your own workspace (whoami returns it). A different workspace is refused.

name: get_workspace_context

description: List the channels of your own workspace that you can see: every public channel, the __dm__ system channel, and the private channels you belong to, sorted by name. Each row has id, workspace_id, name, topic, private, created_at, updated_at and tombstoned_at. Use get_workspace_context to get channels together with threads in one call, and list_dm_conversations for your direct messages. Requires workspace:read.

workspace_id.description: UUID of your own workspace (whoami returns it). A different workspace is refused.

name: list_channels

description: List a parent thread's child threads, oldest first, each as a thread object plus message_count, the number of its live messages. This gives a threaded view of N replies per child without loading any child's messages; tombstoned children are excluded. To read the messages inside a child, call list_messages with the child's id. Requires workspace:read.

thread_id.description: UUID of the parent thread whose children to list. The caller must be able to read the thread's channel.

name: list_child_threads

description: List the messages in a thread, oldest first, excluding withdrawn (tombstoned) ones. Each message has id, author_id, body, metadata, content, posted_at, edited_at and origin. It returns the first limit messages with no cursor, so a long thread's later messages are not reachable here; use get_thread_context for a prompt-ready pack with message cursors and a token budget, or search_messages to find messages by text. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return, counted from the oldest. Defaults to 100; values outside 1 to 500 are clamped into that range.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread whose messages to list.

name: list_messages

description: List a member's per-recipient notifications, newest first. Set unread_only to see just the unread ones. Each carries its kind, thread_id, the thread's title and a short reason read from the event that caused it, enough for a digest line. The durable inbox the notification router fills; drain it here, then wait_for_notification for new ones.
name: list_notifications

description: A channel's threads ordered by last activity — most-recently-posted first. A post floats its thread to the top; a rename does not.
name: list_recently_active_threads

description: List per-target delivery status for a thread's structured result (disposition, external reference, last error). Empty means the result was not routed anywhere, which is valid. workspace:read + thread access.
name: list_result_deliveries

description: List each reviewer's current decision on a thread, ordered by creation time. A row has reviewer_id, decision (approve or request_changes), note, the delegate actor_id if one submitted it, evidence_root, head_sha and dismissed_at, which is set on an approval that a later change request invalidated. Re-submitting replaces a reviewer's row, so earlier verdicts are in list_review_history; whether the requirement is met is in get_review_status. Submit with submit_review. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread whose review decisions to list.

name: list_reviews

description: List thread results in the caller's workspace, newest first. Optional result_kind is an exact-match facet on the namespaced string (e.g. example.review.result/1), not a closed enum. Private-channel rows the caller cannot access are omitted.

result_kind.description: exact namespaced result_kind (e.g. example.review.result/1); omit to list every accessible result

name: list_thread_results

description: List a channel's live threads, oldest first by default or newest first with order=newest, keyset-paginated. Default 100 (max 500); pass cursor=<last thread id of the prior page> for the next page. since (RFC 3339), result_kind and status filter in the query, before the limit.

cursor.description: Exclusive keyset cursor: the prior page's last thread id.

order.description: Direction of the keyset walk (default oldest).

result_kind.description: Only threads whose stored result carries this result_kind.

since.description: Only threads created at or after this RFC 3339 instant.

status.description: Only threads whose declared status is this one (working, needs_input, needs_review, blocked, done).

name: list_threads

description: Move a member's mention inbox read-cursor forward to a given instant, so mentions at or before it count as read, and return the updated inbox: items (up to 50), unread_count and last_read_at. The cursor never moves backward, so an earlier instant than the current cursor changes nothing. This is the cursor for get_inbox; notifications are cleared with mark_notification_read or mark_all_notifications_read instead. The member_id must be the caller. Requires member:self.

member_id.description: UUID of the member whose inbox to advance. It must be the caller's own member id, otherwise the call is refused.

read_through.description: RFC 3339 timestamp, for example 2026-11-25T14:30:00Z. Mentions created at or before this instant are marked read. An instant earlier than the current cursor is ignored.

name: mark_inbox_read

description: Mark one of a member's notifications read (recipient-scoped; marked=false if the id isn't this member's). Requires member:self.
name: mark_notification_read

description: Post a message to a thread as the authenticated member and return the stored message (id, thread_id, author_id, body, metadata, content, posted_at). Send body for plain text or content for typed blocks; when body is empty it is derived from the blocks, and sending neither is refused. A closed thread still takes messages, while a deleted or archived thread refuses them. The post appends a MessagePosted event, records each @handle mention and publishes a mention event for it, and runs the registered slash command when the body begins with /name (see register_slash_command). For a DM conversation id use post_dm_message. Requires message:post.

body.description: Plain-text message text, which is what search indexes; omit when sending typed content, or send an empty string. At least one of body or content is required.

content.description: Typed content blocks in order. Each block has a type: text {text}, code {code, language}, tool_use {id, name, input}, tool_result {tool_use_id, content, is_error}, or resource_link {uri, mime_type, title}. When body is empty, body is built from the blocks; tool_use blocks add no text.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON object stored with the message and returned with it, for example {"artifacts": ["<sha256>"]} to name artifacts the message refers to. Defaults to an empty object.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread to post in. You must be able to read it; a thread in a private channel or DM you are not part of is refused.

name: post_message

description: Search the messages in a workspace by lexical, semantic or hybrid match, best hit first, optionally narrowed by channel, author, author kind and a time window. Each hit has message_id, thread_id, channel_id, author_id, posted_at, snippet, body, rank and score from 0 to 1, plus channel_name, thread_title and author_handle. Private channels and DMs the caller cannot read are never searched. Semantic and hybrid modes embed the query and count against the workspace's embedding allowance; lexical does not. To list a thread's messages in order use list_messages instead. Requires search:query.

after.description: Only messages posted at or after this RFC 3339 instant (inclusive).

author_id.description: UUID of a member. Only messages written by this member are returned.

before.description: Only messages posted before this RFC 3339 instant (exclusive), so together with after it forms a half-open window.

channel_id.description: UUID of a channel. Only messages in this channel are returned.

embedding_model.description: Semantic and hybrid modes only: name of the registered embedding model whose vectors to match against. Defaults to the server's active embedding provider.

hybrid_weight.description: Hybrid mode only: weight given to the semantic score, from 0 to 1, defaulting to 0.5. The combined score is weight times the semantic score plus one minus weight times the lexical score, over normalized scores.

kind.description: Only messages whose author is of this kind: human or agent.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits to return. Defaults to 25, from 1 to 500.

mode.description: How to match. lexical (the default) uses full-text keyword search. semantic embeds the query and ranks by meaning. hybrid blends the two using hybrid_weight.

query.description: The search text, which must not be empty. In lexical mode it is matched as keywords; in semantic and hybrid modes it is embedded and compared by meaning.

snippet_only.description: When true, each hit drops its full body and keeps only the snippet, to save tokens. Defaults to false.

workspace_id.description: UUID of the workspace to search. It must be the caller's own workspace.

name: search_messages

description: Set (upsert) a thread's dispatch priority (G3 fair dispatch). Higher = more urgent (default 0). claim_next orders by an effective rank = this priority aged up the longer the thread waits, so priority jumps the queue without starving long-waiting tasks. Requires thread:transition.
name: set_priority

description: Replace a thread's task attributes in full. The kind says what sort of work it is (change, plan or review), the engine says who or what it is routed to (unattended, session or human), and threat_model marks work that needs a threat model. A claim_next that names an engine takes only work routed to that engine, so an unattended worker is never handed session or human work. A thread nobody described reads as a change with no engine and no threat model.

acceptance.description: how a reviewer verifies the task; the worker must satisfy it

author_family.description: for a review: the provider family that wrote the change under review; claim_next never hands the thread to a claimer of that family. Once set it is kept: a later set neither clears nor changes it

engine.description: omit to leave the work unrouted

lane.description: the service lane it may run in: batch (async, cheapest) or flex; omitted runs at standard rates

linear_issue.description: the Linear issue the task is for, such as ENG-123; where the workspace turned claim comments on, the claim and release are said on it

repo.description: the repository the task changes, as owner/name (a GitHub URL is read as its owner/name); with linear_issue it says which half of a ticket the thread owns, where a workspace keeps [linear_issue, repo] unique

tier.description: the change's review tier; omitted reads as B in the metrics

name: set_thread_attributes

description: Set a thread's persisted steer, the durable guidance a resuming or newly assigned agent should follow, replacing any earlier steer (the latest write wins), and return {thread_id, steer, steered_by, steered_at} with the caller as steered_by. The steer stays on the thread across claims and handoffs and emits no event; a reader picks it up with get_thread_steer. Use it for standing guidance rather than a one-off reply, which belongs in a message. Requires thread:transition.

steer.description: The steering instruction as plain text. It replaces the thread's current steer in full.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread to steer. The caller must be able to read the thread's channel.

name: set_thread_steer

description: Advance a thread's FSM state (start_review, close, or archive). The MCP twin of REST POST /threads/:id. Separation of duties, the required-reviewers close-gate, and unresolved refutes all apply identically — there is no MCP bypass. On a thread with a review requirement, start_review is refused until a result is posted (set_thread_result). Returns the updated thread.

action.description: start_review (open to in_review), close (in_review to closed) or archive (closed to archived). To send work back, use submit_review with request_changes

name: transition_thread

description: Block until you have an unread notification of any kind (a mention, or an event routed to you as owner or follower) and return it with the thread's title and a short reason, or null when the timeout lapses. Use wait_for_mention to wake on mentions only, and list_notifications to read what already waits. It reads the notification ledger, so with since_log_id (the highest source_log_id you have seen) it returns the oldest unread notification after it, including one written while you were not waiting; omitted, only notifications for events after the call count. It never marks the notification read; use mark_notification_read for that. member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.

member_id.description: UUID of the member whose notifications to await. Must be your own member id; another member's id is refused.

since_log_id.description: Return the oldest unread notification whose source_log_id is greater than this, including one written before the call. Omitted, only notifications for events after the call count.

timeout_ms.description: Wait window in milliseconds, from 1 to 300000 (default 30000). When it lapses the tool returns null.

name: wait_for_notification

description: Block until the task named by thread_id produces its result (thread_result_set) and return the result record {thread_id, result, produced_by, produced_at}, or null when the timeout lapses; this is the wait in spawn, wait, aggregate. Unlike the event waits it returns the stored result rather than an event, and it needs a thread_id. A live wait does not see a result that already exists: read it with get_thread_result first, or use get_dependency_results for every dependency result of a parent at once. since_log_id replays a result set on this thread after that log_id before waiting live. To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait. Requires workspace:read.

since_log_id.description: Your high-water log_id. The log is replayed for a matching event with a log_id greater than this before the wait goes live, so an event in the gap between two calls is caught. Omitted, only events after the call count.

thread_id.description: UUID of the task thread whose result to await. You must be able to read it.

timeout_ms.description: Wait window in milliseconds, from 1 to 300000 (default 30000). When it lapses the tool returns null.

name: wait_for_result

description: Return the authentication-bound identity: actor_id, member_id, optional delegation_grant_id, workspace_id, capabilities, capability_sets the caller fully holds, and whether the credential is a bearer. Call this first — writes are attributed to member_id.
name: whoami
